clue.text: In this leader's field, moon offering?

definitions.meaning: read as a race leader's field of vision, which takes in only what is behind
to moon is to bare one's bottom, so what a mooner offers onlookers is a view of the back

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what a leader sees, or what someone mooning puts on show.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves describe a REAR VIEW: the front-runner sees the pack only behind, and a moon shows the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear view is a sight of the back of something, which is all a race leader sees of rivals and all a mooner displays.

clue.text: 3 4 5 15 26 _ : Extrasensory perception is abused by one potterer in ____

definitions.meaning: the novelty glasses promise a sort of second sight, used to peek where one should not
the blank is the letter of the I-spy game, and the answer completes the sentence about a pottering wearer

explanation.surface: A spiritualist complains that second sight is being misused by some idler.
explanation.walkthrough: In each starred clue the answer starts with the letter of the I-spy game, and that first letter is left out of the grid; here the letter is X.
explanation.definitionFit: X-ray specs were a joke-shop novelty sold with the promise of seeing through walls and clothing, a fake kind of super-sight.

clue.text: 3 4 5 15 26 _ : Film dealing with me in another guise

indicators.note: the letters take on a different form, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film about someone in disguise, dealing with the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter, I, is the I-spy letter and is left out of the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: I Am Legend is a 2007 science-fiction film starring Will Smith, from Richard Matheson's novel.

clue.text: One witness might enlighten me — why I only get tip by taking in item's initial, puzzled

definitions.text: One witness might enlighten me — why I only get tip by taking in item's initial, puzzled

indicators.note: a puzzled phrase is jumbled, so all these letters are rearranged
the long string of words takes in one more letter before the whole lot is mixed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone baffled hopes an eyewitness can explain why they only ever get a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the game: one who has seen the thing gives a clue to its first letter, and the other player only gets that initial.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the opening line of the children's guessing game I-spy, where a player names a letter that starts something visible.

clue.text: See 3
See 3
3 4 5 15 26 _ : Show unprincipled blackmailer seizing female

indicators.note: the shortened word grabs the female letter and holds it inside
read as without its principal, so the word for blackmailer loses its first letter

parts.note: an exactor is one who extorts or demands money

explanation.surface: A television show about a ruthless blackmailer who kidnaps a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Unprincipled seems to describe the blackmailer's morals. The I-spy letter X is left out of the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The X Factor is the British television talent contest for singers, created by Simon Cowell.

clue.text: 3 4 5 15 26 _ : Group exercises work on learner — it all stretches me!

indicators.note: the two letters of me are pulled apart round everything else

parts.note: taken as written: its two letters become the outside of the answer

indicators.note: in a down clue the learner sits under, so after, the work

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
op is short for opus, a work
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A class workout session for a novice, who protests that it all stretches them.
explanation.walkthrough: It all is a link: all the other pieces go between M and E. The I-spy letter M stays out of the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: M People were a 1990s British dance-pop band, so a musical group.

clue.text: "He's besotted!" (so off-putting chap might say)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who worships someone blindly
second meaning, split differently: a procrastinator, one who puts things off

explanation.walkthrough: Off-putting here means given to putting things off, not unpleasant; such a person promises I do later, which runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater, strictly a worshipper of idols, is loosely anyone infatuated with or adoring a person.

clue.text: Aussie batsman in 80s cut past backward cover

indicators.note: the cut comes beyond, so after, the reversed cover
the word for cover is to be read from its end to its start

parts.note: to lay is to cover, as with a cloth
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: Cricket commentary: an Australian batsman of the 1980s plays a cut shot past the fielder at backward cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Backward cover and the cut are real cricket terms, so the clue reads as commentary; Graham Yallop batted for Australia in the late 1970s and 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Yallop was an Australian Test batsman who captained his country and played into the mid-1980s.

clue.text: What about puckering pleats for layers of leather?

indicators.note: turned about, so the exclamation is read backwards

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what?

indicators.note: puckered cloth is drawn into new folds, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about crinkled pleats somehow producing layers of leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Heeltaps are the separate layers of leather built up to form the heel of a shoe.

clue.text: Recto-bleeper?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: a recto is a right-hand page
second meaning: a pocket device that beeps to summon someone

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes one odd compound; split it and recto, a right-hand page, gives PAGE R, while a bleeper is the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager is the small radio receiver, called a bleeper in Britain, that beeps to call doctors and others.

clue.text: 3 4 5 15 26 _ : Trance outfit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dream is a trance-like reverie
second meaning: D:..., the 1990s British dance band

explanation.walkthrough: Trance looks like the dance genre but is a dreamlike state; outfit means a band, not clothing. The I-spy letter D stays out of the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is a reverie or stupor, and D:Ream were a pop group who had a hit with Things Can Only Get Better.

clue.text: Dramatist's the reason disheartened singer goes to the country

indicators.note: the singer goes on to, so is followed by, the country word
the reason word loses its heart, its middle letter

parts.note: why? asks for the reason
Cher is the American pop singer
a ley is grassland, the open country of fields

explanation.surface: A dramatist explains why a dejected singer has left town for the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as is. LEY is the farming word for land under grass, standing for the country as opposed to the town.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wycherley was an English Restoration playwright, author of The Country Wife.

clue.text: Chinwag with inmate is wicked

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prison inmate
both wicked and fab are slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A chat with a prisoner is pronounced great.
explanation.walkthrough: Wicked is slang approval here, not villainy.
explanation.definitionFit: A confab, short for confabulation, is an informal chat, which is what a chinwag is in British slang.

clue.text: See 3
Intended to keep the Queen of Hearts'' third note

indicators.note: the word for intended holds the queen inside it

parts.note: meant is to have intended
Diana, Princess of Wales, wished to be a queen of people's hearts; Di is her short name

explanation.surface: Someone meant to keep the Queen of Hearts card and play a third note.
explanation.walkthrough: The playing card is a decoy: Diana, Princess of Wales, said she wanted to be the queen of people's hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: In a musical scale the mediant is the third degree, midway between the tonic and the dominant.

clue.text: 3 4 5 15 26 _ : Global shopping accounts for trouble with alien

parts.note: ET is the film's extra-terrestrial
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Worldwide shopping is blamed for some unrest involving a foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: The I-spy letter E is left out of the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: E-tail is online retail, selling over the internet to customers anywhere in the world.

clue.text: 3 4 5 15 26 _ : Hooker with handcuffs applying ointment — stop here!

parts.note: T.J. Hooker was the police sergeant played by William Shatner in the 1980s American series
unction is anointing with oil or ointment

explanation.surface: A prostitute in cuffs having cream put on is told to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooker suggests a prostitute; it is the TV cop. The I-spy letter T stays out of the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: At a T-junction a minor road meets another head-on, so drivers must halt there before turning.

clue.text: 3 4 5 15 26 _ : Coral reef running round deserted Scottish island inspiring poet

indicators.note: the reef word runs round, enclosing the single letter

parts.note: a cay is a low island or reef of coral
d. is the abbreviation for deserted in military records
Lewis is the northern part of the largest island of the Outer Hebrides

explanation.surface: A coral reef encircling an empty Scottish island gives a poet inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspiring is a link. The I-spy letter C stays out of the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil Day-Lewis was an Anglo-Irish writer who served as Britain's Poet Laureate from 1968 to 1972.

clue.text: The immortal Birdman of Alcatraz initially located in a drug compound

indicators.note: the first letter is placed among the letters of a drug before they are mixed
to compound is to mix together, so these letters are combined into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the prison's name is taken

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Robert Stroud, the Birdman of Alcatraz, is found inside a drug compound.
explanation.walkthrough: The Birdman of Alcatraz is the famous prisoner and film; the real birdman here is Garuda, the immortal bird-man mount of the god Vishnu.
explanation.definitionFit: Garuda in Hindu and Buddhist myth is a deathless creature, part man and part eagle, who carries Vishnu.

clue.text: A hundred quid helps these people practise snobbery

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a quid is a pound, abbreviated L from the Latin libra
assists means helps

explanation.surface: Handing over a hundred pounds lets these people look down on others.
explanation.definitionFit: Classists judge and discriminate by social class, which is the core of snobbery.

clue.text: 3 4 5 15 26 _ : Spot someone who's not somebody

definitions.meaning: the I-spy instruction: pick out a thing starting with the letter
a person ranked at the very bottom of the celebrity lists, a nobody

explanation.walkthrough: Celebrities are ranked A-list downwards, so the last letter of the alphabet marks the least famous. The I-spy letter Z stays out of the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A Z-lister is a minor celebrity of the lowest rank, famous to almost nobody.

clue.text: 3 4 5 15 26 _ : The bare minimum?

definitions.meaning: read literally: what a nearly naked person wears

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for the least you can get away with is read as the least you can wear. The I-spy letter G stays out of the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A G-string is a tiny undergarment covering almost nothing, so it is the barest clothing there is.

clue.text: Where you can get Guinness suitable for slimmers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: your ... is your nearby pub, which serves the Irish stout

explanation.walkthrough: Guinness is an Irish stout; a British local is a neighbourhood pub, and lo-cal is a diet label for low calorie.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is the pub near your home, and lo-cal food has few calories, so both senses share one spelling.

clue.text: Disaffect sergeant, shot to pieces

indicators.note: something shot to pieces is broken up, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Turning troops against a sergeant who has been gunned down.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to alienate them, turning their affection or loyalty away, which is what disaffecting does.

clue.text: See 3
As a prospect, compete and finish first when cycling?

indicators.note: cycling sends the closing letters round to the front, rotating the joined words

parts.note: to vie is to compete
to win is to finish first

explanation.surface: A cyclist sees the chance to race and come first as a real prospect.
explanation.walkthrough: Cycling looks like the sport but signals moving letters round from one end to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in view is foreseen or expected, a likely prospect in the future.

clue.text: Receiving a French city

parts.note: per means a, as in a pound per head
Nancy is a city in Lorraine, north-east France

explanation.surface: Being welcomed to a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: PERNANCY is a rare legal term, so the wordplay carries it: per as in so much a head.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernancy is a legal word for the taking or receipt of profits or rents from land.

clue.text: Spiny anteaters administered "earwigging" in back of stable

indicators.note: the scolding word goes inside the reversed word for stable
the word for stable is taken from the back, so read in reverse

parts.note: sane means mentally stable
an earwigging is a scolding, and to have given one is to have chid, the old past tense of chide

explanation.surface: A telling-off given to animals at the rear of a horse stable.
explanation.walkthrough: Back of stable suggests a stable's last letter; it means stable's synonym written backwards. Earwigging is British slang for a reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: Echidnas are egg-laying Australasian mammals with spines, also called spiny anteaters.
